countries.name: Germany
countries.blurb: Tuition-free public universities, Ausbildung apprenticeships, and strong post-study work options.

metrics.ielts: Often not if German program / MOI / university test; English programs may ask IELTS/TOEFL
metrics.low_marks: Medium — Ausbildung & some pathways more flexible than elite unis
metrics.part_time_work: 120 full days or 240 half days/year (typical student rule — verify)
metrics.post_study: 18-month job seeker (study) / skilled work after Ausbildung
metrics.language: German A2–B1 often for Ausbildung; English for many degrees

costs.amount: Often ~€11,000+ for first year — confirm current amount

suits: Students seeking low/no tuition public universities
Applicants aiming for paid Ausbildung (nursing, IT, trades, hospitality)
Professionals targeting skilled worker visas with recognition
Profiles ready to plan blocked account (Sperrkonto) funds
refusals: Insufficient or unexplained funds / blocked account gaps
Weak study motivation or unclear program fit
Language level not meeting Ausbildung employer needs

faq.q: Is Germany tuition free for international students?
faq.a: Many public universities charge little or no tuition — usually a semester contribution (~€150–€350). Private universities cost more. Living costs and blocked-account proof still apply. Embassies decide visas; SK Immigration does not guarantee outcomes.

faq.q: Can I do Ausbildung without perfect German?
faq.a: Employers typically expect A2–B1 German (sometimes higher for nursing). You can start language training while preparing the file. SK Immigration helps with CV, matching and document checklists.
A blocked account proving you can cover living costs for a study visa. Amounts and banks change — always verify current embassy guidance.
